note: Literature links biallelic TBC1D32 variants to retinal disease as a major postnatal feature alongside hypopituitarism, contrasting with lethal fetal malformations.

evidence.text: A review of reported TBC1D32 ciliopathy cases identified retinal disease, facial dysmorphism, and hypopituitarism as major clinical features, with phenotypic manifestations ranging from isolated retinal disease to severe multisystemic involvement and fetal demise.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and molecular spectrum of TBC1D32-related ciliopathy: case reports and literature Review
source.quote: A review of previously reported cases highlighted facial dysmorphism, retinal disease, and hypopituitarism as major clinical features of TBC1D32-related ciliopathy.

evidence.text: TBC1D32 variants show a wide spectrum that includes retinal dystrophy and reduced visual acuity in surviving patients, alongside severe life-limiting congenital anomalies in fetal probands.

source.title: Diagnosis of TBC1D32‐associated conditions: Expanding the phenotypic spectrum of a complex ciliopathy
source.quote: We provide additional data to expand the phenotype correlated with TBC1D32 variants, including a severe prenatal phenotype associated with life-limiting congenital anomalies.
